visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video opens with a wide shot of the Makishi Public Market entrance in Naha, Okinawa. A large digital LED screen above the entryway displays vibrant food advertisements. Several pedestrians are seen walking through the bright, airy entrance area. The architecture is modern with clean lines and high ceilings. Multiple text overlays in pink and white introduce the market. (2) The scene transitions to a high-angle interior view of the market, revealing organized rows of vendor stalls with consistent pink and white signage. The floors are clean and reflective under bright, uniform indoor lighting. Shoppers are seen scattered throughout the aisles, browsing various goods. The environment appears fresh and recently renovated. (3) The camera focuses on the seafood section, showing clear tanks filled with live crabs, lobsters, and large shellfish. Specific shellfish like 'night-light snails' are showcased in close-up. The water in the tanks is agitated by oxygenators, and the products are presented on ice or in labeled containers. Bright lighting highlights the textures of the shells and wet surfaces. (4) A segment features meat stalls, specifically 'Uehara Meat Shop,' where counters are filled with various cuts of red meat, including marbled beef and pork. Shop employees are visible behind glass counters wearing professional white uniforms and masks. The display is well-lit, emphasizing the quality and color of the meat products. (5) The footage moves to a tofu specialty stall, showing a hand holding a small piece of white tofu on a wooden stick. Packaged 'Ji-mami Tofu' in plastic cups with red and black branding is shown prominently. The setting includes traditional fabric banners (noren) and retail shelves filled with packaged local goods. (6) The camera browses 'Oshiroy' and 'Ayumi' stalls, which are packed with colorful jars of seasonings, sauces, and local snacks. The visual density is high, with shelves and baskets overflowing with inventory. Lighting remains bright, and the camera uses close-ups to highlight specific product packaging and shop signage. (7) The scene shifts to the outdoor covered market street, 'Ichiba-hondori,' where many small shops line a pedestrian thoroughfare under a curved glass roof. The camera explores 'Matsubara Confectionery,' showing a variety of traditional Okinawan fried donuts and pastries displayed on trays. A final shot shows the camera descending an escalator into a busy ground-floor market area before ending on a social media contact screen.

It serves as an informative guide recommending three must-visit stalls and highlighting regional specialties like Ji-mami tofu, seafood, and Sata Andagi donuts.
